title: C_Finalize: document why memset(g_slots) before thread join is safe
description: In C_Finalize, memset(g_slots, 0, sizeof(g_slots)) happens at line 2411, while pthread_join for USB/flash/fsdir background threads happens later (lines 2445/2467/2492). On first read this looks like a UAF window. It is actually safe because: (1) g_lock is held during the memset so no background thread can be inside the lock-protected g_slots access; (2) g_lock_ready is set to 0 before WP11_UNLOCK(), so any thread that subsequently acquires g_lock will fail WP11_LOCK() and exit without touching g_slots. The pthread_joins then confirm the threads have fully exited before wc_FreeMutex. Fix: add an inline comment at the memset(g_slots) call explaining the invariant, so reviewers do not re-flag this as an ordering bug.
